title: FM27 Mods — Real Names, Logo & Face Packs
description: FM27 mods: what lands in the first weeks after 10 November, which FM26 packs carry over, the install order that works, and the compatibility rules that break most installs.
meta: Football Manager 27 mods — what is version-locked, what carries over, and the install order that works.
body:
No FM27 mods exist on 22 October 2026. Mods are built against a shipped build: the folder tree, the config format and — for anything touching the database — the save format itself. FM27 launches on 10 November, so this page is the compatibility map you need before the download links start appearing.

What "mods" means in Football Manager

Five different things get called a mod, and they age very differently:

  • Real names and licensing fixes — restore real competition, club and award names. Database-level, so version-locked.
  • Graphics packs — logos, kits and player faces. Image files plus a config file, so the least version-sensitive family.
  • Skins — interface replacements, rebuilt whenever panels move. Covered on the FM27 skins page.
  • Data updates and editor files — transfer updates, custom leagues, edited databases. Locked to the game version that reads them.
  • Tools — scouting and editing utilities that read a save file. They break when the save format changes, and they break hardest.

Why the first weeks after launch look like this

The FM26 download area on FM Scout carries around 690 files and is still being updated in 2026 — the FM26 real names fix still carried a March 2026 update and sits among the most-downloaded files in that area. That tells you where demand sits: names first, faces and logos next, tools last.

Expect the same order for FM27. A real names fix cannot exist until someone can read the FM27 database, which means after the launch build or a late Launch Preview. Graphics packs can be assembled earlier, because most of the artwork is reused.

What carries over from FM26

  • Logos and kits: usually yes. Existing packs are image files, and guides to FM26 graphics describe earlier packs working after small adjustments — the adjustment being the folder layout and the config file, not the artwork.
  • Faces: yes, with the same caveat. Season-specific face megapacks need a new season release before they are useful.
  • Real names fixes: no. A fix written against the FM26 database does not patch the FM27 database.
  • Editor files and custom databases: no. They are built for a specific game version and will not load cleanly into the next one.
  • Skins: no, not without a rebuild.
  • Tools: no, until the tool author ships an FM27 build.

Install order that avoids the usual failures

  1. Launch the game once so it creates its user-data folder, then confirm the FM27 folder name inside Sports Interactive.
  2. Drop graphics into the graphics subfolder, one folder per pack, keeping the pack's internal folder structure intact.
  3. Check the config file — a pack without a valid config will show nothing even when every image is in the right place.
  4. Clear the cache, then reload the skin with caching off. Skipping this is the most common reason a correct install looks broken.
  5. Verify in-game on a club whose badge you know, before you install the next pack. One change at a time is the only way to find the thing that broke it.
Back up the saves subfolder before installing anything that touches the database. Graphics are reversible; a half-applied data update is not.

The FM27 week-one checklist

  • Day one: nothing. Play the launch build and confirm what is actually missing — FM27 adds a fully licensed Arkema Première Ligue, and licensing changes shift what a names fix needs to cover.
  • First week: logo pack, face pack, one skin — the three that are safe and reversible.
  • After the first patch: real names fix and any editor data, once they are rebuilt against the shipped database.
  • Never: a data update from a different game version, or an FM26 tool pointed at an FM27 save.

What this page will not do

No rehosting of other people's files. No "FM27 mod" label on an FM26 pack with a renamed title. Every entry will name the version it was built for and the date it was checked.
